title: Voyager 1 — the first machine a light-day from Earth (Nov 18, 2026)

segments.en: November eighteenth: the first machine ever to be a light-day from Earth.
segments.en_cap: Nov 18: | the first machine | ever to be a light-day | from Earth.

segments.en: Look back. The Sun is just a star, right below Orion.
And Earth? Lost in the glare. The Sun outshines ten full Moons.
segments.en_cap: And Earth? | Lost in the glare. | The Sun outshines | 10 full Moons.

segments.en: A signal from Earth reaches the Sun in eight minutes. Jupiter, forty-three. Saturn, over an hour. Neptune, four hours.
segments.en_cap: A signal from Earth | reaches the Sun | in 8 minutes. | Jupiter, 43 min. | Saturn, over an hour. | Neptune, 4 hours.

segments.en: Voyager one: soon, a full light-day.
Saturn's gravity bent its path north, out of the plane of the planets.
segments.en_cap: Saturn's gravity | bent its path north, | out of the plane | of the planets.

segments.en: Twenty-twelve: it left the Sun's bubble.
Nuclear-powered, yet it calls home with about twenty-three watts: a fridge light bulb.
segments.en_cap: Nuclear-powered, | yet it calls home | with about 23 watts: | a fridge light bulb.

segments.en: All six computers together hold about sixty-eight kilobytes. Bolted to its side: the Golden Record.
segments.en_cap: All 6 computers together | hold about 68 kilobytes. | Bolted to its side: | the Golden Record.

segments.en: In about forty thousand years, it'll drift within two light-years of a small red star. But first, mark the date.
segments.en_cap: In about 40,000 years, | it'll drift within | 2 light-years | of a small red star. | But first, mark the date.
